title: Report on the Grey Ear
author: Reeve Haldric Millbrook
pages: To my lord, from the Reeve of Millbrook, Dimming. The grey ear is in the south fields. The wheat stands grey and light in the hand, black spots at the stem. It smells sweet-sour, like old bread.
It came, I think, on sacks from the Kingsway market. The two farms that bought seed there have it worst. I have burned their fields, as the Grovewarden advised. They wept. I had to.
Grain is nine pence and climbing. Twelve families have no stores for Deepnight. I have opened the parish stores early. I beg my lord to remit the Tenth Sheaf this year, or there will be a rising.
Strangers from the blighted south arrive daily. Some of our people want the gates shut. The Flamekeeper reminds them of Bowl-Right. I side with her. Hungry folk turned away do not go away.
Postscript. A soup kitchen has opened by the old chapel, run by quiet folk in grey. They feed everyone. The Flamekeeper does not like them. I cannot afford to dislike anyone who feeds my people.
